section_summary.extract_value: This section describes the statistical analysis plan: SPSS v23 was used for descriptive and Pearson correlation analyses among BMI, social safeness (SSPS), body appreciation (BAS-2), inflexible eating (IEQ), and disordered eating (EDE-Q); AMOS was used for path analyses testing whether body appreciation and inflexible eating mediate the relationship between social safeness and disordered eating while controlling for BMI. The section does not report sample descriptors (e.g., country, sample size, mean age, percent white, mean BMI), survey method, the method of BMI assessment, actual correlation coefficients, or study numbering.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'The software IBM SPSS Statistics (version 23.0; IBM; Chicago, IL, USA) was used to conduct descriptive and correlational analyses.'; 'Pearson product-moment correlation analyses were performed to explore the relationship between BMI, social safeness (SSPS), body appreciation (BAS-2), infexible eating (IEQ) and disordered eating (EDE-Q).'; 'Furthermore, to calculate the presumed relationships between study variables a series of path analyses were conducted with the software "analysis of momentary structure" (AMOS; [40])... In this model, BMI was considered a confounding variable and its effect was controlled for.'
